## 02b21c59893a

**Finding A1 — production lesson can omit the source-anchor concept.**  Generator
SHA-256 `deba97398b956509f404419c72fb6fee06b52801a684fe8ac6537601162dc6f6`;
canonical rule hash `ba8a3944ecbc`.

With `difficulty=medium`, seed `861`, and sample indices `0..4`, the production
generator emits blue-anchor counts `[0,0,0,0,1]`.  Treating indices 0–3 as the four
demonstrations and index 4 as the query, an “always use origin (0,0) as source”
rival matches all four Racket-authoritative demonstration outputs and differs from
the query answer at four cells.  This is a legal no-override production sample,
not a hand-built off-domain input.  The exact five inputs, canonical outputs,
rival query, hashes, and command are retained in
`checks/audit/02b21c59893a/no-blue-shortcut/counterexample.json`; the supported
Racket receipt is
`checks/audit/02b21c59893a/no-blue-shortcut/racket.json`.

Secondary checks agree that the target is not acceptance-ready: lint fails because
`RULE_HASH` is missing; defect lint reports texture-domain overlap, a minimal
self-check impostor, and undeclared lawful degenerates; the required semantic gate
cannot assess rotations because no semantic contract is declared; and override
checking fails with silent unknown-key acceptance and many advertised-domain
rejections.  Evidence is under `checks/audit/02b21c59893a/`.

**Suggested repair direction, not applied:** use a deterministic lesson schedule
that guarantees at least two blue-anchor witnesses among the demonstrations,
declare the always-origin rival, add an executable identifiability hook, pin the
canonical rule hash, and make override domains match per-band realizability.
